verdict_text:
NO

The artifact drops blocks {2, 5, 9} instead of the specified {2, 5, 8}, violating "Required result" clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 5, 8"). As a consequence the renumbering is also wrong: it maps old 8→6, old 10→7, old 11→8, whereas clause 2 mandates old 9→6, old 10→7, old 11→8 (and old 8 must not survive at all). Everything else — the pattern-based whole-block matching, contiguity check, the 121-tensor assertion, and writing `out/T1/model.safetensors` only after the checks pass — conforms, and the tensor count still comes out to 121, so the error is silent by count and only caught by the hidden reference's bit-exact key/value comparison. The `assert` statements would also be stripped under `python -O`, which weakens the "fail loudly" requirement, but that is secondary to the wrong block set.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
